rule.description: A function whose body absorbed the implementations of a multi-level sub-method call chain: one body simultaneously carries extreme statement mass (>=70 statements), control-flow nesting depth (>=4), and raw length (>=110 lines), a combination no single well-scoped function in this repository reaches.

checks.description: Detect functions whose bodies are carrying the copied implementations of an entire depth-3-or-deeper helper call chain, so the function performs the same computation in one oversized body instead of delegating to well-scoped sub-methods at the former abstraction levels.
checks.detected_relation: function <- absorbed inline copy of its multi-level sub-method call chain
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The monolithic body holds the logic of helpers that belong at narrower scopes; helper ownership boundaries are lost inside one function, which is the defining relation of a deeply inlined method. The structural combination of statement mass, nesting depth, and length is the direct footprint of pasting a 3-plus-level pipeline into one body, and is calibrated so that no function of the clean repository satisfies it.

matches.evidence: The single-test command handler carries, in its own body, the steps that used to be separate responsibilities: parsing the Python source, walking the parse tree to enumerate test functions and reconstruct their suite-qualified names, probing the interpreter for the configured test framework, and building and driving the terminal session.

The shared formatting pipeline that every formatter subclass enters now performs, inline, the temp-file lifecycle, cancellation checking, executable and module resolution, error reporting, and a full re-implementation of the unified-diff decoder used to turn formatter output into workspace edits.

The inlay-hints provider single-handedly decides which hint kinds the configuration enables, whether a hint position falls in the requested range, races the hover and signature-help requests against their timeouts, and converts those responses into hint labels inline.

The flake8 provider no longer delegates to the shared provider pipeline: its own method configures the executable, decides stdin versus file invocation, spawns and drains the child process, decodes the line protocol into messages, and maps per-type severities, duplicating what the shared base class and the per-provider info object used to own.

The document diagnostics engine folds into one method the eligibility decision (settings toggles, language identity, ignore patterns, file existence), the per-product provider construction that a factory method used to own, and the message-to-diagnostic mapping including its quote-based column correction.

The whole import-sorting pipeline lives in the command function itself: temp-file creation beside the original file, sorter executable and argument resolution, an inline copy of the python execution service's spawn, decode and stderr policy, and a full unified-diff decoder replayed against the document, ending in the workspace edit application.

excluded.reason: Long registration entry point (111 statements) but flat wiring glue (maxNesting 2): it registers commands and providers in sequence rather than absorbing a sub-method call chain, so it does not meet the structural relation.

Legitimately dense, single-purpose diff-decoder helpers in the utility module. They delegate across one level and stay below the statement threshold; they are the original owners of decoding logic that flagged sites absorbed, not instances of the smell themselves.
A focused module-level helper with a single responsibility (create the sidecar temp file); small in every dimension and kept as-is by the case.
